refnamediv.refpurpose: Set read file buffering on the given stream

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.parameters;
stream
The file pointer.
size
The number of bytes to buffer. If size is 0 then read operations are unbuffered. This ensures that all reads with fread are completed before other processes are allowed to read from that input stream.
Only fread and fgetc honor a size of 0: fgets and stream_get_line still read ahead. A read filter on the stream overrides it, data that is already buffered is kept, and a later non-zero size switches the buffering back on. For a user-space stream wrapper, the call is only forwarded to streamWrapper::stream_set_option, so reads are not unbuffered.

&reftitle.returnvalues;
Returns 0 on success, or -1 if the request cannot be honored, which only happens when the streamWrapper::stream_set_option method of a user-space wrapper returns &false; or is missing. Many streams (php://memory, php://temp, directory handles) do nothing and still return 0, so 0 does not mean that the buffering changed.
